headline: Use {arm:beta}, provisionally: of the arms inside both bars it gets the total right most often, but this run cannot separate it from the cheaper {arm:gamma}.
lede: {arm:beta} leads {arm:gamma} by {aspects.answers.pair.beta.gamma.change|pts} points on the right total, an interval that reaches below zero, while {arm:alpha}, the strongest answerer, misses both bars. If a larger run shows the lead is noise, {arm:gamma}, cheaper and faster, becomes the pick.
flag: Only the cost and turn-time bars were set in advance. Nothing declared how often an arm must get the total right, or what a point of it is worth.

caveats.material_if: the lead of the arm picked shrinks on fresh cases, as the best of a few tends to; then the cheaper and faster arm is the pick
the owner values the cheaper arm's lower cost or turn time inside the bars, or needs a minimum answer rate; either ranks the arms inside the bars differently from answering alone

a paired read over the shared cases moves the beta-against-gamma verdict; today's corrected pair interval already reaches below zero, so pairing could only firm up or dissolve the lead, not reverse the bar verdicts
the queued backlog differed between arms' runs; the extractor trades thoroughness for speed under backlog, so it would move both turn time and answer rate, the two things this call rests on
a different grader tolerance or key scored one arm's runs, moving its answer rate with no change in what it extracted
a different OCR build fed one arm's runs, so a missed total was never legible to it
a different model played the user for one arm's runs
the simulated user ran with a different output cap or reasoning budget for one arm's runs
the simulated user's calls were sent with different request settings for one arm's runs
one arm saw cleaner scans than another
one arm saw documents in a language its field labels don't match
handwritten annotation differed between arms' documents
the adjudicated template graded against differed between arms' runs
a payment hold was in force from the first turn for one arm and not another
operator corrections arrived at different points for different arms
supervisor sign-off differed between arms' runs, changing what the goal check reads

caveats.id: unreported:orchestration_ms (llm_ms, tool_ms were not measured, so the parts cannot account for the whole.)
caveats.material_if: a fix needs to know which part of the turn is slow; the bar reads whole-turn time, which is measured, so the call does not rest on the parts

decision.text: Use {arm:beta}. It clears both bars and gets the total right in {pass_rate.beta|pct} of trials, the most of any arm that clears them. Nothing separates it from {arm:gamma}, and the campaign's own rule for an unseparated pick falls back to cost, which would choose {arm:gamma}. This report departs from that rule because the question ranks answering inside the bars, and a saving the bars already allow buys nothing it asks for.

{arm:alpha} costs {scoreboard.alpha.reply_cost_usd|usd_per_1k} against a bar of {criteria.answers/bar/cost_usd.threshold|usd_per_1k}, and misses the turn-time bar too, each by its whole interval. Its answer lead over {arm:beta} is not separated either ({aspects.answers.pair.alpha.beta.interval|interval} points).

{arm:gamma} is cheaper and faster, and the pipeline's dominance reading favours it over {arm:beta} for that reason, since nothing separates them on answering. It gets the total right in {pass_rate.gamma|pct} of trials, and both arms sit inside the bars, so its saving is not what the question ranks.

Turn time is {arm:beta}'s nearest line: {weakest.margin} under the bar on its mean, and its p95 reaches {measure.total_ms.beta.p95}. If today's gap is the true one, a rerun of today's size still reads {arm:gamma} ahead {settle.beta.gamma.goal_state:reply.total == case.total.overall.wrong_side|pct} of the time.

A larger run of {arm:beta} and {arm:gamma} on fresh cases, the same cases for both, at today's {repeats|int} repeats each: about {settle.beta.gamma.goal_state:reply.total == case.total.overall.cases_needed_80|int} trials per arm separates them in most such runs if today's gap is real. Repeating today's {cases|int} cases more often does not count toward it.

claims.text: {arm:alpha} misses both bars by its whole interval; {arm:beta} and {arm:gamma} clear both.

claims.text: Inside the bars, {arm:beta} gets the total right more often than {arm:gamma}, but the corrected gap of {aspects.answers.pair.beta.gamma.change|pts} points reaches below zero ({aspects.answers.pair.beta.gamma.interval|interval}); the chart shows each arm's own spread, not that gap.

evidence.caption: Share of trials with the right total, with each arm's own interval. The corrected gap between arms has no chart; the sentence above carries it.

evidence.caption: Both checks per arm as a share of trials, with intervals.

explore.outcome: Lowering the bar under {scoreboard.beta.reply_cost_usd|usd_per_1k} leaves {arm:gamma} the only arm inside. Raising it to {scoreboard.alpha.reply_cost_usd|usd_per_1k} does not admit {arm:alpha} alone, since it also misses the turn-time bar.

A bar that cuts into or below {arm:beta}'s interval ({aspects.answers.bar.total_ms.beta.interval|interval}) but stays above {arm:gamma}'s ({aspects.answers.bar.total_ms.gamma.interval|interval}) leaves {arm:gamma} the only arm inside; below {arm:gamma}'s, no arm qualifies. {arm:alpha} needs a bar above {aspects.answers.bar.total_ms.alpha.interval|interval}.

Read on each arm's estimate, a floor between {pass_rate.gamma|pct} and {pass_rate.beta|pct} leaves {arm:beta} the only arm inside the bars that meets it, and a floor above {pass_rate.beta|pct} leaves none, since {arm:alpha} misses both bars. Read on whole intervals, as the bars are, no floor separates {arm:beta} from {arm:gamma}: their intervals overlap.

method.text: {cases|int} cases, each run {repeats|int} times per arm, {scoreboard.beta.ran|int} trials per arm; intervals are over cases, not trials.
A trial passes when the reply's total matches the case total. Citing the policy is checked too, and every arm passes it every time.

Each arm's rate carries its own interval at {spread.beta.goal_state:reply.total == case.total.overall.level}. Differences between arms are corrected across every pair of arms, read at {aspects.answers.pair.beta.gamma.confidence}.

The question asks which arm answers within the cost and turn-time bars, so both bars rule options out here. The pipeline reads bars as warnings, so every arm survives there; it has {arm:gamma} dominating {arm:beta} and {arm:beta} dominating {arm:alpha}, each on cost with answering not separated, while {arm:gamma} does not dominate {arm:alpha}, which is ahead of it ({aspects.answers.pair.alpha.gamma.interval|interval} points). This report removes {arm:alpha} on the bars and ranks answering above cost inside them, which is why it picks {arm:beta} over the pipeline's cost tie-break.

How often a rerun reads the other arm ahead assumes today's gap is the true one. It sizes a rerun's risk, not the evidence that {arm:beta} is ahead, so the pick does not rest on it and it sits in Watch.
The trials needed to separate two arms count trials as fresh cases at today's repeats, read as independent arms; a paired read on shared cases needs fewer.
Spend per reply across all roles, which equals production cost per reply for every arm.
No arm is a control; arms compare in pairs.
